q8.answer: Counts live in one shared Redis, in a key per customer per window, rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}, so every gateway instance reads and increments the same number. Each key is given an expiry at the window end plus a 5 second margin, so old counters remove themselves.

q9.answer: Budget returns to zero when the next wall-clock minute window begins, because the counter key includes windowStart and a new window means a new key. It is a fixed window aligned to wall-clock minutes (from Redis TIME), the same for every customer, not a rolling or per-customer-start window.

q10.answer: The check and increment run as a single Lua script on Redis (EVAL), which executes atomically. It reads the count, rejects if count >= limit, otherwise INCRs, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.

q11.answer: The Lua script computes it from Redis time as the seconds left in the current window (windowEnd - redisTime), rounded up and at least 1, and returns it to the gateway, which sends it as Retry-After. The count resets at the next window, so retrying after that long succeeds.

q12.answer: No retry: the gateway makes one attempt with a 50 ms deadline, then forwards the request, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable once, and adds no X-RateLimit headers. There is also no local fallback counter and no circuit breaker.
